title: Lenny Rachitsky: How to know you have product-market fit, benchmark retention, and plan growth for a Series A
summary: Lenny draws on research into successful companies to explain three signs of product-market fit, retention benchmarks by business type, and a four-engine growth framework. He also covers 10 ways startups found their first thousand users, all aimed at a Series A raise.

principles.text: Product-market fit means a real market exists; look for sudden pull, gradual compounding pull, or flattening cohort retention curves.
principles.quote: you look for a sudden and significant pull from the market or gradual but compounding pull from the market or and or actually uh your cohort retention curves flatten

principles.text: Retention is the ultimate PMF measure: if the cohort curve flattens above zero, a segment wants your product.
principles.quote: if that curve flattens out and doesn't drop to zero you have product market fit with some segment of the market

principles.text: Track retention by cohort, not blended monthly churn, so you can see whether product changes actually helped.
principles.quote: the other approach blends together new users and existing users and you can tell if changes to your product are having an impact because you don't know what percentage of those are new

principles.text: Good retention benchmarks vary by business type, scaling with acquisition cost and customer stickiness.
principles.quote: the cost to acquire users scale basically linearly through this list so with the consumer social spectrum it's very cheap to acquire snapchat user and instagram user very expensive to acquire an enterprise

principles.text: Your growth is driven by one of four engines (paid, content, sales, virality); pick the best fit and master it.
principles.quote: there's only one of these four engines is going to be responsible for the majority of your growth so it's really important that you figure out which of these engines is most likely to drive your growth

principles.text: Don't mistake one-off turbo boosts like PR for a self-sustaining engine; invest in the engine itself.
principles.quote: mistake a lot of founders make is they rely on these things again and again and again thinking it's going to drive their growth ongoing without investing in their engine
